name: Penicillin G sodium
executiveSummary: Crystalline benzylpenicillin IV. Adult: moderate infections ~2–4 MU every 4–6 h; severe/meningitis up to 18–24 MU/day. Pediatrics 100,000–400,000 IU/kg/day by severity.
indications:
## Indications

- Infections due to susceptible gram-positives (streptococci, some non–penicillinase-producing staphylococci) and susceptible *Neisseria*.
- Susceptible pneumococcal pneumonia, streptococcal endocarditis, syphilis (IV regimens), meningococcal/pneumococcal meningitis, gas gangrene in combination.

## Precautions

- Penicillin allergy. Seizures at high doses or in uremia.
- Sodium content clinically relevant at high doses.
- Avoid antagonism with bacteriostatics (tetracyclines, chloramphenicol, erythromycin) when bactericidal effect is required.

> Do not confuse with benzathine (IM depot) or procaine penicillin.

adulto.dose: Mild–moderate: **2–4 MU/day** divided every 4–6 h. Severe: **12–24 MU/day** in divided doses every 4–6 h or continuous infusion per institutional regimen. Neurosyphilis: often **18–24 MU/day**. Meningitis: high-dose every-4-h regimens.
adulto.administration: Prefer intermittent IV: dilute (e.g. 3 MU in 100 mL NS) and infuse 15–60 min. IV push only small volumes over 3–5 min if the label allows — avoid rapid boluses of high doses.
adulto.notes: Adjust in renal failure. Monitor Na⁺ and renal function at high doses.

pediatrico.dose: Mild–moderate: **100,000–150,000 IU/kg/day every 6 h** (max **8 MU/day**). Severe: **200,000–300,000 IU/kg/day every 4 h** (max **24 MU/day**). Meningitis: **300,000–400,000 IU/kg/day every 4 h**. GBS meningitis: **450,000–500,000 IU/kg/day every 6 h**. Congenital syphilis: < 7 days **50,000 IU/kg every 12 h**; days 8–30 **every 8 h**; > 1 month **every 4–6 h**.
pediatrico.administration: IV; usual concentration 100,000–500,000 IU/mL (infants ~50,000 IU/mL); 15–60 min with pump.
pediatrico.notes: Always calculate in IU/kg. Confirm susceptibility (pneumococcal resistance).

neonatal.dose: Orientative non-meningitic: **50,000 IU/kg/dose every 12 h** in neonates. Meningitis / syphilis: more frequent intervals by gestational and postnatal age.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted / diluted: usually up to 48 h refrigerated (check label).
- Pediatric cards often allow up to 7 days refrigerated for some dilutions — confirm brand.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Rash, urticaria, fever, eosinophilia, hemolytic anemia, leukopenia. High dose/uremia: seizures. Anaphylaxis.
